A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LEGO-Learn. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and added appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original ID classification and OOD detection experiments on four graph datasets, including component ablations and filter comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results for label budgets, alternative class partitions, variability, filter weights, and OOD score distributions.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same weighted C+1 GCN filter, ID classifier training, K-Medoids selection with uncertainty ranking, annotation cycle, and entropy-based OOD detection. The additional experiments do not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ID classification and OOD detection on Cora, AmazonComputers/Amazon-CS, AmazonPhoto, and LastFMAsia. The additional class partitions and label budgets vary settings within these retained datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain all twelve combinations of GCN-ENT, OODGAT, and GNNSafe with random, uncertainty, FeatProp, and MITIGATE selection. The new appendix comparisons use the existing GCN-ENT comparator family; no new comparison method is documented.

E3.justification: The main sampling design and 15×C label budget remain. v2 adds 10×C and 20×C budgets, alternative Cora/LastFMAsia class partitions, and additional filter-weight settings. Section 4.1.3 and Appendix B change FPR@95 to FPR@80, although existing FPR values remain identical; this establishes a reported metric change, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, selection-precision analysis, and strong-filter comparison, v2 adds budget sensitivity, robustness to alternative ID/OOD class partitions, a six-value filter-weight sweep, and an ID/OOD score-distribution diagnostic in Appendices C and E–G. These substantially broaden the supplementary validation.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged over ten random seeds. v2 newly reports standard deviations for four metrics for LEGO-Learn and GCN-ENT on Cora and LastFMAsia in Table 10. It does not document increased run counts or introduce significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing main, precision, filter, and ablation tables retain their numerical values. New Tables 8–12 and Figure 3 add budget, partition, variability, weight-sensitivity, and score-distribution outcomes. For example, Table 11 reports alternate-partition Cora AUROC of 0.9210 for LEGO-Learn versus 0.8290 for GCN-ENT, not a same-setting improvement over v1. Table 12 also reports 0.7800 accuracy at w=0.1, differing without explanation from the retained 0.7810 normal-filter result in Table 4.

T1.justification: The transductive problem formulation, objectives, mathematical definitions, and Equations 1–12 remain substantively unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the first label-efficient graph open-set learning claim, the purity–informativeness contribution, and the four-dataset effectiveness claims, including the headline 6.62% accuracy and 7.49% AUROC improvements. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: The new appendices interpret alternative class-partition results as evidence of generalizability, standard deviations as evidence of stability, and score separation as evidence of effective discrimination. Existing explanations of over-filtering and the purity–informativeness trade-off, together with the future-work boundaries, remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly provides a code-repository location after the contributions in Section 1. The previously documented architectures, cluster count, learning rate, dropout, and validation-based weight selection remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes the LMN discussion and Huang et al. (2022) reference, and the GPA discussion and Hu et al. (2020) reference. It adds two Xu et al. graph-similarity references from 2020 and 2021. The broader positioning against graph active learning and image-based open-set annotation remains.

P1.justification: v2 makes local prose edits and clarifies the selection objective and node-set descriptions in Section 3.1 while retaining the main section sequence. It reorganizes the appendices, incorporates the former precision appendix into Section 4.3, adds Mengyuan Li to the author list, and adds acknowledgments.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column ACM layout to a predominantly single-column TMLR layout. Figure 2 is redrawn, the precision bar chart is removed while its underlying table moves from Appendix C to Section 4.3, and five new appendix tables and an OOD-score figure are added. Existing FPR table headings also change.

improvement.justification: v2 improves assessment of the unchanged method through additional budget and class-partition checks, quantitative uncertainty reporting, and a code-access pointer. These address limited validation and reproducibility gaps in v1. The gain is constrained by the unexplained FPR@95-to-FPR@80 revision with unchanged values, sparse details for some new comparisons, and the inconsistent w=0.1 accuracy across Tables 4 and 12.
